head_commit.message:
fix: certify organize-appai at the app level, not via mantle repo-invariants

The certification workflow's final step ran `python -m mantle certify`,
which executes mantle-os's repository-invariants. Several of those
(SPORE-2, FRICTION-1, GHNEST-13, GHNEST-17) assert properties of the
mantle-os *source* repository - docs/MANTLE2_CONSOLIDATION_MATRIX.md,
src/mantle/nest, spore lifecycle receipts, audit workflow templates -
none of which exist in (or apply to) the organize-appai application repo,
so every certification job failed at that step.

Add scripts/certify_app.py, which runs certify_nest(include_invariants=False)
to certify the resident app at the application level, and point the
workflow's 'Application certification' step at it. Artifacts from the local
certification/demo runs are gitignored.

Verified: app-level certification passes (stage1 passed: True, no failed
codes) and produces a valid signed receipt.

head_commit.message:
fix: resolve mypy type errors blocking the tests workflow

Once the mantle skip-guard let pytest pass, the mypy step surfaced a backlog
of pre-existing type errors in the mantle-2 migration code. Fix all of them:

- rule.py: type collection as All | Any (HasFilterPipeline had no .filters)
- cli.py: type sinks as list[TraceSink] (held JSONLSink + MantleSink)
- why.py: add report_events() typed accessor; use it in assist.py, cli.py and
  test_explain_why.py instead of iterating dict[str, object]['events']
- assist.py: widen filters to list[dict | str]; write proposal via open()
  (Path.write_text has no newline= under the python_version=3.9 mypy config)
- terminal.py: annotate _feed/_ask/_record and cast the bound method

Verified: mypy clean, ruff clean, 295 passed / 8 skipped (no mantle),
299 passed / 4 skipped (with mantle, certification path).

head_commit.message:
fix: skip mantle tests cleanly when mantle not installed; make demo.sh executable

- tests/appai/test_terminal.py: gate the 4 mantle-dependent tests behind a
  requires_mantle marker so the plain tests.yml workflow (which does not
  install the mantle2 extra) skips them cleanly instead of failing with
  ModuleNotFoundError. They still run fully in the certification workflow,
  where mantle-os is installed.
- pyproject.toml: add mantle/mantle.* to the mypy ignore_missing_imports
  list (mantle-os ships no py.typed stubs).
- scripts/demo.sh: set the executable bit (was committed 100644, causing
  the certification workflow's demo.sh step to fail with exit code 126).

head_commit.message:
fix: test teardown removed a symlink with os.rmdir (NotADirectoryError on POSIX)

The real Linux failure was in the test's cleanup: finally: link.rmdir() calls
os.rmdir, which raises NotADirectoryError (ENOTDIR) on a POSIX symlink. Remove the
link with unlink() on POSIX (rmdir remains correct for Windows junctions). This is
the actual cause of the persistent test_containment_rejects_symlink_escape CI
failure; the containment logic change is a defensive hardening on top.

head_commit.message:
fix: resolve parent only when checking containment (no NotADirectoryError)

The earlier os.path.realpath(full path) still hit Path-level NotADirectoryError on
the Linux runner for a symlink escape with a non-existent leaf. Resolve ONLY the
candidate's parent (a real directory, so realpath cannot raise) and append the leaf
name as a pure string op. This still resolves the parent through the escaping
symlink, so a link pointing outside the approved root is refused as ContainmentError,
while legitimate contained paths and symlinks that stay inside still pass.

head_commit.message:
deps: bump mantle-os pin to @main for the grimoire pip-install fix

The Windows certification step (mantle certify) crashed with FileNotFoundError for
documents/grimoire/editions/grimoire-v0.10.md under the Python Lib dir. That was a
mantle-os packaging bug (paths.REPO_ROOT collapsing to <prefix>/Lib when pip-
installed) fixed upstream in mantle-os main (PR #39: grimoire source checks skip
cleanly when not a checkout). Point the direct CI install and the mantle2 extra at
@main so organize-appai picks up the fix.

display_title: fix: containment must not crash on symlink escape (NotADirectoryError)

head_commit.message:
fix: containment must not crash on symlink escape (NotADirectoryError)

require_contained used Path.resolve(strict=False), which on some platforms raises
NotADirectoryError for a symlink-to-directory whose leaf does not exist, turning a
containment refusal into a crash (observed as the failing
test_containment_rejects_symlink_escape on the Linux CI runner).

Use os.path.realpath instead: it follows symlinks leniently and never raises for a
symlink escape with a non-existent leaf, so the real path is resolved and the
refusal is reported as ContainmentError. Verified against all containment cases:
parent/absolute escape refused, symlink escape refused, symlink that stays inside
still allowed, plain subpaths allowed.
